paragraphs.source_en: A parable: The Monk and the Minister

units.source_en: A parable: The Monk and the Minister

paragraphs.source_en: Two close boyhood friends grow up and go their separate ways. One becomes a humble monk, the other a rich and powerful minister to the king.

units.source_en: Two close boyhood friends grow up and go their separate ways.
One becomes a humble monk, the other a rich and powerful minister to the king.

paragraphs.source_en: Years later they meet. As they catch up, the portly minister (in his fine robes) takes pity on the thin and shabby monk. Seeking to help, he says:

units.source_en: As they catch up, the portly minister (in his fine robes) takes pity on the thin and shabby monk.

ja.t: は、やせてみすぼらしい

paragraphs.source_en: “You know, if you could learn to cater to the king, you wouldn’t have to live on rice and beans.”

units.source_en: “You know, if you could learn to cater to the king, you wouldn’t have to live on rice and beans.”

paragraphs.source_en: “If you could learn to live on rice and beans, you wouldn’t have to cater to the king.”

units.source_en: “If you could learn to live on rice and beans, you wouldn’t have to cater to the king.”

paragraphs.source_en: Most all of us fall somewhere between the two. As for me, it is better to be closer to the monk.

units.source_en: Most all of us fall somewhere between the two.

ja.t: たちのほとんどは、この
